steps.description:
Previously, you explored sequencing with the Buzzer module, learning about rhythm and sound effects. In this unit, you'll dive into Concurrency, meaning making multiple actions happen together. But first, let's learn about the LCD module.

The LCD block is used to display text on the LCD. You can type in the "Display Text" box of the LCD block.


Using an LCD block, display the text "This is way too long" for 3 seconds.
Notice that the text is cropped? As the LCD has only 16 columns, make sure your text can fit in next time!

Previously, you explored sequencing with the Buzzer module, learning about rhythm and sound effects. In this unit, you'll dive into Concurrency, meaning making multiple actions happen together. But first, let's learn about the LCD module.

The LCD block is used to display text on the LCD. You can type in the "Display Text" box of the LCD block.

Besides typing directly into the LCD block, you can use the Number and Text blocks.


You will notice that you can insert the Text block into the LCD "Display Text" but not the Number block (because it is not a text).


To resolve this, we use the Create-text-with block to convert values to text in order to display it on the LCD.


You can also join blocks into a single row with the Create-text-with block. Try out this example and observe the display.


Of course, you can simply type all the content into the "Display Text" of the LCD but we'll see why the Create-text-with block is so important later on.
